title: Dev Spark Sprint — Messaging & Econ Lab
body:
Goal: produce 3 compact developer-first message tracks + 4 pricing microcopy variants for a 1-click quickstart flow that maximizes time-to-first-infer and early retention. Run two A/B tests in the next sprint (webflow and signup-email).

Context / hypothesis:
- Developers value speed & predictability over feature laundry lists at first touch.
- Primary friction points: unclear billing, long model warmup, and sample code that doesn't run in <60s.
- If we can prove a 30–60s first inference with clear per-request cost anchors, activation conversion will climb.

Audience: early-stage startups + platform engineers evaluating hosted endpoints. Persona hooks: "get from repo to token in 10 minutes", "cost predictable for dev proof-of-concept", "no infra ops required to scale from prototype to 1k qps".

Topline Value Propositions (short, dev-friendly):
- Instant inference: "From zero to first token in under a minute — example code included."
- Predictable economics: "Per-token pricing + per-call estimates so engineers can budget features, not guesses."
- Production-ready defaults: "Autoscaling, KV cache, and fallback models out of the box — your dev prototype runs like a product."

Three message tracks (for A/B testing):
Track A — "Speed-first":
- Headline: "Launch an LLM feature in 10 minutes"
- Subhead: "Example app, 1-line SDK, live keys. First inference in <60s."
- CTA: "Try the 10-minute quickstart"
- Hero microcopy: "No infra, no config. Just call /v1/infer and stream results."

Track B — "Cost-clarity":
- Headline: "Know the price before you ship"
- Subhead: "Token & embedding meters with realistic cost estimates per use-case."
- CTA: "Estimate your feature cost"
- Hero microcopy: "We show per-call cost in the console and SDK — no surprises on invoices."

Track C — "Product-ready":
- Headline: "Prototype today, SLA tomorrow"
- Subhead: "Autoscaling pools, model rollouts, and logs built for production."
- CTA: "Get dedicated dev capacity"
- Hero microcopy: "Start small, scale predictably — same API as our Dedicated offering."

Quickstart flow (developer UX):
- Landing -> "Try the 10-minute quickstart" -> create project (prefilled sample code) -> copy API key -> run sample curl or Node snippet -> see streaming tokens + cost estimate for that call -> optional: save as template.
- Snippets (concise): curl example, node fetch, python requests. Each snippet shows a predicted cost line like: "Estimate: ~0.0008 USD for this request".

Pricing-language experiments (4 variants):
- P1 (Explicit per-token anchor): "$0.00003 / token (gen models); $0.00002 / token (embed). Estimate per call shown in console."
- P2 (Per-feature friendly): "Small prototype pack: 100K tokens free, then pay-as-you-go. See per-call meter in console."
- P3 (Unit-based simplify): "1 inference unit = 1K tokens. 0.03 USD / unit. Use units to model cost in your app."
- P4 (Outcome-framing): "Expect 1–3¢ per generated paragraph (typical). See exact per-call price." 

Recommended microcopy experiments (homepage & quickstart):
- Billing on-boarding modal: "Estimated cost for this run: 0.0012 USD — this will be billed to your trial credit first."
- Post-infer toast: "Success — tokens used: 184 • cost: $0.0055 (view details)": shows transparency.
- Price note in SDK: "Pricing estimates sent with each response are advisory; final bill rounds at 100 token granularity."

Competitor callouts (short notes for sales/engineers):
- Major cloud managed endpoints: strong on single-vendor ops & infra but vague on unit economics for token-heavy workloads; selling point vs them: explicit per-call meters + unit experiments for devs.
- LLM API incumbents: often simpler UX but higher default cost; selling point: production controls (rollouts, fallback) without extra config.
- Self-hosted runtimes: cheaper at scale but require weeks of setup; selling point: plug-in to hosted API first, then port to Private/Dedicated when needed with consistent API.

Suggested analytics/KPIs to measure (for experiment success):
- Activation funnel: sign-up -> headline CTA click -> key generated -> first inference success (goal: 60% of clicks complete a successful inference)
- Time metrics: time-to-first-infer (target < 60s), time-to-first-meaningful-output (target < 90s)
- Cost transparency metrics: % of users who view per-call estimate before calling (goal 50% first week)
- Conversion: trial -> paid (compare tracks over 14 days)

Risk notes / unknowns:
- Token-language complexity: per-call estimates are noisy for streaming/function-calls — need engineering guardrails.
- Warmup variability across regions/hardware may break the <60s promise sometimes; build a soft SLO and public-facing language: "typically under 60s for sample models".

Next steps (owner: Claire):
- Implement copy A/B for homepage hero + quickstart CTA (launch 2/10).
- Wire the per-call estimate into the sample snippets and front-end (eng ticket: github:rw-infer/console#423).
- Draft in-product microcopy for billing modal and SDK comments (owner: Aisha).
- Run first cohort test with devhub email list (sample: 1k signups) and record metrics.

Open questions (working notes):
- Do we show precise per-token math in the header or hide under "estimate" toggle?
- Should we promote "starter pack 100K tokens" or leave it as trial credit only?

Notes to designers/engineers (sketchy):
- Design: small inline cost chip under call-to-action; hovering shows breakdown (model, tokens, estimated cost).
- Engineer: include a simulator endpoint that returns a pre-run estimate so the UI can show cost before the actual call.

Quick copy bank (one-liners for banners, emails, CTAs):
- "Ship your first LLM call in under a minute — sample app included."
- "No surprises: see the cost of each request before you run it."
- "Prototype quickly, operate reliably — same API from trial to SLA."

Measurements and timeline:
- Week 1: implement hero A/B + quickstart microcopy (design + small front-end). Start tracking time-to-first-infer.
- Week 2: enable price estimates in snippets, run cohort test.
- Week 3: analyze activation, pick winner, roll into broader homepage copy.

Raw brainstorm fragments (leave as-is):
- "developer friction = time + surprise billing". 
- "little code that runs" > 10x better than docs that only show concepts.
- consider a "cost estimator" plugin for the SDK that devs can call locally to approximate costs.

Owner notes: keep copy lean and instrument everything. The signal we'll optimize for is reduction in time-to-first-infer and increase in conversion to paid over 14 days.
